A creative learning community
Welcome to Hankham Primary School.
Welcome to Hankham Primary School, a small school with big ambitions.
We pride ourselves on a nurturing, family feel where every child is seen, heard, and truly known. We prioritise positive relationships and a safe, happy environment, where everyone knows your name, creating a seamless support network between home and school.
Our "family feel" extends far beyond our village borders. While we are a small school, we hold big, global ambitions for our pupils, ensuring they grow up as curious and connected citizens of the world. We are incredibly proud of our international partnerships, which bring the world into our classrooms. Through long-standing links with partner schools in Germany, Poland, and the Czech Republic, our children engage in meaningful cultural exchanges that broaden their horizons and build lasting friendships. Whether through collaborative projects or shared learning experiences, these European connections ensure our pupils understand their place in a diverse global community.
Whether your child is starting school for the first time, moving from another area, or moving from infant to junior phase, the best way to appreciate our lovely school is to see it in action. Please contact the school office on 01323 763265 or use our online booking form below to schedule a tour.
If you have any queries in the meantime please feel free to call us.
Hankham Primary School Tour – Fill in form
We look forward to meeting you!
Sarah Timlin - Headteacher

Starting School
We run regular open days for parents looking for a school place for their child, which are advertised here and on the home page. We also accept in-year admissions where we have space, so if you are looking for a school place please do get in touch with our friendly school receptionist, Mrs Moore, to make an appointment to view the school.
Your child's journey to school starts at home
We understand that all children develop at their own pace, and that we’re all learning from birth. When it’s time to start school, some children will need more help than others.
There are key skills* that schools expect children to be learning before their first day. Practising these will make your child’s journey to Reception as positive as possible.
If your child is already at nursery, in pre-school, or with a childminder, those professionals will work with you and your child to help get them ready.
There’s lots you can do at home to build your child’s confidence and independence, helping them feel emotionally and practically prepared to start school.

All children need help from their trusted adults to feel confident and excited about starting Reception.

English
At Hankham, we develop a love of reading and writing through a variety of fun and engaging activities to enhance the curriculum. These include: author visits, World Book Day and mixed age reading partners. We also promote the Library Summer Reading Challenge.
We are also involved in the UN's Sustainable Development Goals Book Club. Stories can fuel children's imagination and raise awareness of new possibilities. The SDG Book Club aims to encourage young people across the world to learn about the SDGs in a fun, engaging way and help them realise what actions they can take, empowering them to make a difference.
We follow a phonics programme, the DfE approved Twinkl phonics programme, which focuses on Systematic Synthetic phonics teaching, . Each year group is taught separately with a discrete daily Phonics lesson with additional phonic activities throughout the week. EYFS focus on Levels 2, 3 & 4 while Year 1 focus on Level 5 and Year 2 focus on Level 6 . Letter formation is also a focus with pre-cursive in EYFS and cursive from Year 1.
At Hankham, the teaching of reading skills is an integral part of our English lessons. Reading skills, including children’s decoding and fluency, as well as a rich vocabulary, are also developed through teaching across the curriculum areas. We use Reading VIPERS to focus on key reading skills throughout the week (Vocubulary, Infer, Predict, Explain, Retrieve, Sequence). In addition, reading comprehension is taught throughout the school through the use of the scheme Cracking Comprehension.
Regular intervention reading groups take place to support those children who need additional support with reading. Specific reading interventions are put in place to focus on individual needs.
We encourage the children to access a range of enriching texts to develop good comprehension and foster a love of reading. Reading Champions in Year 6 help to promote the love of reading throughout the school and help look after our fantastic library.

Physical Education
Physical Education at Hankham is an important way in which we support our children's physical and mental wellbeing. Hankham is involved in many inter-school competitions with other local primary schools. We have an outdoor gym for the older children and a 'Daily Mile Track' which the children use every day to complete their daily mile.

The Arts
The Arts at Hankham - art, dance, drama, music - all help to engage the children and support with confidence and wellbeing.
As a school, we incorporate art and culture into every child's learning. Previously an Artsmark panel commended us particularly as a school for our work improving "mindfulness and wellbeing through the Arts."
The school also drives much of its international dimension through the Arts.

pageCache.text:
Vision and our curriculum intent
We strive to prepare our children for active citizenship. We follow the National Curriculum and what is taught, is driven by the UN Sustainable Development Goals. At Hankham we highlight to the children how the knowledge and skills covered throughout our various curriculum areas are linked and interdependent and how they support and promote the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). These goals are incorporated across all areas of the curriculum, help drive and shape our curriculum themes and activities and prepare the children to be effective global citizens in the 21st Century.Click here to find out more about the Sustainable Development Goals.
~ A creative learning community ~
We encourage everyone to be aware of and to understand our place in the local and wider community, including the wider world.
We encourage children to be mindful of their thoughts and feelings and those of others, and to connect and develop positive relationships with family, friends and with people from similar and different backgrounds.
We encourage everyone to play an active role in our community, through both smaller and larger acts.
We strive to provide everyone at Hankham with the skills, knowledge, values and creativity to connect and work with others to make our world more equal, fair and sustainable and to keep themselves and everyone else happy, healthy and safe.
We encourage everyone to find a sport or physical activity they can regularly enjoy to support their physical and mental wellbeing.
We promote the enjoyment of and participation in the Arts to improve self-confidence, mindfulness and wellbeing.
We encourage everyone to develop a lifelong love of learning to improve one’s sense of achievement and to encourage self-challenge and resilience.
